text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency breach detected for streaming endpoints in eu-west-2. Auto-page sent to on-call. Metrics: p95=320ms, p99=1.8s, streaming tail errors increased by 12% over baseline. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/example/panel/streaming-eu-west2

maria: I’m on it — seeing correlated increase in socket timeouts and stream stalls. Repro: small replay on internal test client shows tail stalls at ~1.7s.

oncall-bot: Paging raj (netops) and ingrid (sre) — escalate after 5m if no ack.

raj: Ack. looking at VPC egress metrics and NAT metrics for eu-west-2. Initial thought: ephemeral port exhaustion or cross-AZ routing flaps.

ingrid: I can confirm TLS handshake RTTs spiking in eu-west-2: SNI handshakes showing 3-4x retransmits, packets with dup acks. Sample from tcpdump:```15:23:12.345678 IP a.b.c.d.443 > x.y.z.w.49152: Flags [S.], seq 1, ack 1, win 65535``` then many `SYN` retries.

raj: netstat summary from nat-gw-3: `tcp_time_wait: 120000, ephemeral_in_use: 50200/65535` — close to exhaustion. Also seeing NAT translation table churn.

maria: p95/p99 on the downstream egress path show increased queueing between AZb->AZc. traceroute shows hop 3 latency spike intermittently. Looks like cross-zone routing jitter.

netops-bot: Detected increased NAT translation churn on nat-gw-3 (eu-west-2a). Suggested actions: rotate nat-gw, increase ephemeral range.

raj: Temporarily reassigning a subset of traffic off nat-gw-3 to nat-gw-1 in eu-west-2b. Command:```aws ec2 replace-route --route-table rtb-xxxx --destination 0.0.0.0/0 --nat-gateway-id nat-0aaa``` applying to 20% of subnet CIDRs now.

maria: Pushing canary reroute to 20% — monitoring. Streaming tail p99 dropped from 1.8s -> 900ms within 90s for canary traffic. :thumbsup:

olivia (cs): Heads-up — we have two enterprise customers seeing degraded transcripts. I’ll open inbound tickets and post an update to their boards: "We are investigating cross-zone egress latency impacting streaming; mitigation in progress."

ingrid: While reroute helps, TLS handshake retransmits persist upstream. I’m seeing DNS query spikes with servfail from internal resolver in AZb. Possibly rate-limited or overloaded.

raj: Increasing NAT ephemeral port range on nat-gw-3 as a mitigation and rotating resolver group for AZb. Steps: 1) scale nat-gw-3 elasticpool (increase ports) 2) add additional resolver instances 3) reduce per-instance client ephemeral port reuse. Doing 1 now.

maria: Applying short-term runtime mitigations for streaming: enable prefix KV caching and reduce batch window from 40ms -> 20ms for affected routes to lower open connections. Patch command:```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://console.redwood/api/route/config -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","batch_ms":20,"kv_cache":true}'```

ingrid: After NAT port increase and resolver rotation, seeing TLS retransmits drop ~60%, DNS SERVFAILs drop. p99 continues to hover ~700-900ms but trending down.

sre-lead: Good. Can we capture a short postmortem checklist here for follow-up? Need root cause hypothesis, permanent mitigations, and customer comms.

raj: Root cause hypothesis: combination of NAT ephemeral port exhaustion on nat-gw-3 + transient resolver CPU pressure in AZb causing DNS latency and TLS handshake retransmits; cross-AZ routing jitter amplified tail latency for streaming.

maria: Long-term mitigations I propose: 1) split NAT load across more gateways in eu-west-2, 2) bump ephemeral pool defaults for high-throughput subnets, 3) add proactive NAT churn alerting and backpressure when ephemeral_in_use > 70%, 4) add DNS resolver autoscale policy for sudden qps spikes.

ingrid: Also recommend adding a streaming-specific fallback: if tail latency > p99 threshold for 3m, switch streaming sessions for new connections to a lower-concurrency model variant (reduce per-connection resource demand) to preserve tail.

olivia (cs): I posted a brief customer update: "Mitigation in place; traffic rerouted and NAT capacity increased. Monitoring for full recovery. Will follow up with postmortem." Customers acknowledged.

netops-bot: nat-gw-3 ephemeral range increased to 70000, resolver-group rotated.

maria: Final checks: p95=220ms, p99=640ms, streaming error rate back to baseline. Marking incident as mitigated in thread. Will create formal incident doc and assign to eng-infra for follow-up items.

oncall-bot: Incident mitigated by on-call. Please file postmortem ticket and tag `incident:networking` and `priority:high` for follow-up.

sre-lead: Thanks everyone. Handing off to morning shift for remediation work and postmortem. I’ll take postmortem ownership.

maria: noting runbook updates required: add NAT ephemeral alert, add resolver autoscale playbook, and document streaming fallback config.

ingrid: saving packet captures and logs to s3://redwood-incidents/3419994321/ for postmortem.

olivia (cs): I’ll follow up with affected customers with a timeline and mitigation summary.

maria: closing thread — create follow-up tickets, assign owners, and schedule 1hr blameless postmortem tomorrow. :white_check_mark:
